papers.title: Single-cell multiomic mapping of genetic predisposition to childhood B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia
papers.authors: Lee, A. J., Neehus, A.-L., Wahlster, L., Agarwal, G., Weng, C., Zhang, A., Liu, T., Shelton, S., Ye, T., Volpe, L. d., Cohn, O., Poeschla, M., King, E., Ha, S. A., Turvey, A. K., Chiang, C. W. K., Wiemels, J. L., de Smith, A. J., Sankaran, V. G.
papers.abstract: Inherited genetic variation substantially increases the risk for developing childhood B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL), the most common cancer in children, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. To address this limitation, we employ a single-cell multiomic framework to functionally dissect common regulatory variants associated with B-ALL risk. Coupling this multiomic an
summary_bullets: Single-cell multiomic analysis reveals how inherited genetic variants associated with B-ALL risk affect gene regulation in developing B cells.
Common regulatory variants alter chromatin accessibility and gene expression patterns, mechanistically linking genetic predisposition to childhood leukemia development.
Multiomic framework enables functional dissection of disease-associated variants at single-cell resolution, improving understanding of B-ALL genetic risk mechanisms.

papers.title: Mitotic adaptations shape acquired resistance and vulnerabilities to KIF18A inhibition in cancer
papers.authors: Klaasen, S. S. J., Vukusic, K., van Gerven, M. M. R., van Attikum, H., Tolic, I. M., Luijsterburg, M. S. M.
papers.abstract: KIF18A inhibition selectively kills cancer cells by inducing chromosome alignment defects that activate a spindle assembly checkpoint (SAC)-dependent mitotic arrest. The mechanisms by which initially sensitive cancer cells acquire resistance to KIF18A inhibitors (KIF18Ai), the vulnerabilities of resistant cells, and the initial genetic determinants of KIF18Ai sensitivity remain poorly understood.
summary_bullets: Cancer cells acquire KIF18A inhibitor resistance through mitotic adaptations that bypass spindle checkpoint arrest mechanisms.
Resistant cells develop new vulnerabilities exploitable by combination therapies targeting alternative mitotic pathways.
Specific genetic factors predetermine initial sensitivity to KIF18A inhibition in cancer cells.

papers.title: Fanconi Anaemia E3 Ligase complex activity is regulated by a druggable metabolite binding site in FANCX
papers.authors: Sharp, M. F., Gee, Y. S., Luu, J., Cowley, K., Beetham, H., Langendorf, C. G., Oakhill, J. S., Scott, J. W., Cavero, D., Minguillon, J., Che, D., Baell, J. B., Deans, A. J., Surralles, J., Simpson, K. J., Crismani, W.
papers.abstract: The Fanconi anaemia (FA) DNA repair pathway is an emerging target for precision cancer therapy. Using a high-throughput FANCD2-monoubiquitination assay, we identified a class of small molecules, including MSG010, that inhibit the FA E3 ligase complex in vitro. Because these molecules, and the metabolite, palmitoyl-CoA, are known to engage allosteric drug and metabolite (ADaM) binding site in AMP-a
summary_bullets: FA E3 ligase complex activity is regulated by a druggable ADaM binding site in FANCX that binds metabolites like palmitoyl-CoA
Small molecule inhibitors (MSG010) targeting this site suppress FANCD2 monoubiquitination, offering precision therapy for FA-associated cancers
Metabolite-binding regulation of DNA repair pathways represents a druggable vulnerability for cancer treatment

papers.title: A functional genomics screen of human B-cell differentiation reveals convergent mechanisms of inherited childhood leukemia predisposition
papers.authors: Wahlster, L., Neehus, A.-L., Lee, A. J., Mazumder, S., Mehrzad, P., Black, S., Messa, L., Liu, T., Wang, C., Weng, C., Caulier, A., Pak, J., Fleming, T., Antoszewski, M., Zhang, A., Ha, S. A., Oleaga-Quintas, C., de Smith, A. J., Sankaran, V. G.
papers.abstract: B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) is the most common childhood cancer, yet the mechanisms by which inherited risk variants predispose to leukemia development remain poorly understood. A major challenge to studying these mechanisms has been the lack of model systems that faithfully capture the transient developmental states in which predisposition alleles are thought to act. Here, we esta
summary_bullets: Functional genomics screen identifies convergent mechanisms linking inherited B-ALL risk variants to disrupted B-cell differentiation pathways.
Predisposition alleles act during transient developmental states, revealed through novel model systems capturing early B-cell development stages.
Multiple inherited risk variants converge on shared molecular mechanisms, suggesting common pathways underlying childhood leukemia susceptibility.

papers.title: Engineered caspases directly rewire mutant Ras to cell death
papers.authors: Moeller, L., Lu, A. C., Ho, K., Zhang, E., Elowitz, M. B.
papers.abstract: As central executioners of cell death, caspases that activate exclusively in diseased cells would provide powerful and specific therapeutic agents. Natural caspase regulation exhibits two universal features that facilitate the engineering of such caspases: proximity-induced subunit assembly and modular separation of substrate recruitment from catalysis. Here, we take advantage of these features to

papers.title: SLIM: A small linear model with STRING embeddings for single-cell genetic perturbation prediction
papers.authors: Hu, D., Pielies Avelli, M., Jensen, L. J., Rasmussen, S.
papers.abstract: Predicting cellular responses to genetic perturbations is central to understanding gene function and prioritizing therapeutic targets, but experimental screens cannot exhaustively cover genes, cell types, and perturbation combinations. Recent benchmarks have shown that simple baselines can match or outperform substantially more complex models, suggesting that informative biological priors may be a
summary_bullets: Simple linear models with STRING protein interaction embeddings effectively predict single-cell genetic perturbation responses.
Biological priors from protein networks match or exceed performance of complex deep learning approaches.
SLIM provides computationally efficient alternative for perturbation prediction across genes and cell types.

papers.title: A confound-diagnostic toolkit for in silico perturbation with single-cell foundation models
papers.authors: Qiu, R., Zhao, M. M.
papers.abstract: Deleting a gene token from a cell's input sequence offers a convenient native strategy for in silico perturbation, but the resulting embedding delta may not represent a biological knockout response. Apparent effects can instead reflect gene identity, universal responsiveness, limited tokenization coverage, library-size contamination, or circular state scoring. Here, we present a confound-diagnosti
summary_bullets: Gene token deletion in foundation models may reflect confounds (gene identity, tokenization artifacts) rather than true biological knockout effects.
Toolkit diagnoses whether embedding changes represent genuine perturbation responses or statistical/technical artifacts in single-cell models.
Critical for validating in silico predictions before biological interpretation or experimental validation.

papers.title: Benchmarking single-cell foundation models in a zero-shot setting
papers.authors: Gaballa, Y., Ahmed, S., Abdelaal, T.
papers.abstract: Single-cell foundation models have recently emerged as a promising approach for learning general-purpose representations from large-scale transcriptomic data. These models are trained on millions of cells and are designed to transfer their learned representations to a wide range of downstream tasks. However, their practical benefits compared to traditional approaches are still not fully understood
summary_bullets: Single-cell foundation models show limited zero-shot transfer advantages over traditional methods in most tested downstream tasks.
Larger pre-training datasets don't consistently improve performance on unseen cell types or conditions.
Foundation model effectiveness varies significantly by task type, with unclear generalization patterns across applications.

papers.title: Myeloid-targeted RNA nanotherapeutics rewire cholesterol metabolism to unleash anti-tumor immunity in glioblastoma
papers.authors: Huo, J., Lin, H., Li, Y., Tripathi, S., Chojak, R., Silvers, C., Peng, Y., Boland, L., Zhang, J., McCortney, K., Perera, R. M., Najem, H., Billingham, L. K., Chia, T.-Y., Chen, X., Wang, H., Sun, J., Siringan, M. J., Jing, L., Musabji, A., Congivaram, H., Wang, S., Lopez-Rosas, A., Kumthekar, P., Jamshidi, P., Ahmed, A. U., Lee-Chang, C., Chandler, J. P., Youngblood, M. W., Sonabend, A., Tate, M. C., Shah, H., Thorp, E. B., Lesniak, M. S., Heimberger, A. B., Miska, J., Zhang, P.
papers.abstract: Tumor-associated myeloid cells (TAMCs) dominate the glioblastoma (GBM) microenvironment and suppress anti-tumor immunity. Here, we identify cholesterol efflux via ABCA1 as a targetable metabolic checkpoint controlling TAMC immunosuppression in GBM. Reprogramming TAMC cholesterol metabolism using TAMC-targeting lipid nanoparticle encapsulating ABCA1 siRNA (ABCA1 LNP) converts TAMCs into potent anti
summary_bullets: ABCA1-mediated cholesterol efflux represents a key metabolic checkpoint controlling immunosuppression in tumor-associated myeloid cells in glioblastoma.
Myeloid-targeted LNP-ABCA1 siRNA reprograms cholesterol metabolism to convert immunosuppressive TAMCs into anti-tumor effector cells.
This metabolic rewiring approach enhances anti-tumor immunity and represents a novel therapeutic strategy for glioblastoma.

papers.title: CagA delivery by the Helicobacter pylori Cag-Type IV Secretion System confers fitness benefits and costs during stomach infection
papers.authors: Snow, J., Frick, J., O'Brien, V. P., Guo, C., Gray-Owen, S. D., Salama, N.
papers.abstract: Helicobacter pylori strains encoding the cag-pathogenicity island (cag-PAI) and the effector toxin cagA are associated with worse disease outcomes. The cag-PAI encodes the Cag type IV secretion system (Cag-T4SS) which injects CagA and other bacterial products into gastric epithelial cells. Prior work revealed that host adaptive immunity promotes recombination in the cag-PAI gene cagY to attenuate
summary_bullets: Cag-PAI delivery in H. pylori confers both fitness advantages and costs during stomach infection
Host adaptive immunity drives recombination in cagY, suggesting immune-mediated selection against virulence factors
CagA toxin injection provides complex evolutionary tradeoffs during chronic gastric infection

papers.title: YAP-TEAD-driven CPA4 promotes NF2-deficient meningioma growth
papers.authors: Mineji, K., Petrosky, K., Otsuji, R., Makino, Y., Kibe, Y., Uchida, E., Hagita, D., Singaravelan, N., Ishi, Y., Yamaguchi, S., Chang, L.-S., Gadd, S., Hashizume, R.
papers.abstract: Neurofibromin 2 (NF2) deficiency is a driver of meningioma and other cancers, yet transcriptional effectors that sustain NF2-deficient tumors remain poorly defined. We identify carboxypeptidase A4 (CPA4) as an effector of YAP-TEAD signaling in NF2-deficient meningioma. Transcriptomic profiling identified CPA4 as a consistently upregulated effector. Across patient cohorts and specimens, CPA4 expres
summary_bullets: YAP-TEAD signaling drives CPA4 expression in NF2-deficient meningiomas, identifying a key transcriptional pathway sustaining tumor growth.
CPA4 is consistently upregulated across NF2-deficient meningioma patient samples and represents a potential therapeutic target.
CPA4 functions as a YAP-TEAD effector that promotes meningioma development downstream of NF2 loss.

papers.title: Cell size reduction distinctly scales spindle elongation and chromosome segregation in C. elegans.
papers.authors: Okafornta CW, Farhadifar R, Fabig G, Wu HY, Köckert M, Vogel M, Baum D, Haase R, Shelley MJ, Needleman DJ, Müller-Reichert T.
papers.abstract: How embryos adapt their internal cellular machinery to reductions in cell size during development remains a fundamental question in cell biology. Here, we use high-resolution lattice light-sheet fluorescence microscopy and automated image analysis to quantify lineage-resolved mitotic spindle and chromosome segregation dynamics from the 2- to 64-cell stages in Caenorhabditis elegans embryos. While
summary_bullets: Cell size reduction scales spindle elongation proportionally, maintaining proper chromosome segregation despite decreasing embryo volumes.
High-resolution imaging reveals mitotic spindle dynamics adapt systematically across developmental stages as cells progressively divide.
Chromosome segregation fidelity is preserved through coordinated scaling of spindle machinery with cell size changes.

papers.title: Explainable AI: learning from the learners.
papers.authors: Vinuesa R, Brunton SL, Mengaldo G.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence now outperforms humans in several scientific and engineering tasks, yet its internal representations often remain opaque. In this Perspective, we argue that explainable artificial intelligence (XAI), used alongside causal reasoning and domain validation, enables learning from the learners. Focusing on discovery, optimization and certification, we show how foundation models
summary_bullets: XAI combined with causal reasoning and domain validation enables extracting scientific insights from AI systems outperforming humans.
Explainable AI supports discovery, optimization, and certification tasks by making opaque internal representations interpretable.
Foundation models can teach researchers by revealing learned patterns when properly explained and validated.

papers.title: The next Turing tests: Reimagining conceptions and measures of AI.
papers.authors: Hernandez-Orallo J, Collins KM, Cheke L, Weidinger L, Bhatt U, Griffiths TL, Cave S.
papers.abstract: New approaches to evaluating progress of AI should be built around diversity, partnership, and systemicity.
summary_bullets: Current AI evaluation methods need reimagining beyond traditional benchmarks; future approaches should emphasize diversity, partnership, and systemic assessment.
AI progress evaluation requires collaborative frameworks that test systems across varied contexts rather than isolated tasks.
Systematic, multi-stakeholder evaluation approaches better capture real-world AI capabilities and impacts than single standardized tests.

papers.title: Generative design of bacteriophages with genome language models.
papers.authors: King SH, Driscoll CL, Li DB, Guo D, Merchant AT, Brixi G, Wilkinson ME, Hie BL.
papers.abstract: Many important biological functions arise not from single genes but from complex interactions encoded by entire genomes. We report the first generative design of complete bacteriophage genomes using genome language models. We generated viable bacteriophages with target host tropism, using the phage ΦX174 as our design template. Experimental testing yielded 16 phages with diverse fitness profiles i
summary_bullets: First generative design of complete bacteriophage genomes using language models, creating viable phages with target host specificity.
Demonstrated that genome-level language models can encode complex biological functions beyond single genes.
Generated 16 distinct phages with diverse fitness profiles, validating computational design approach experimentally.

papers.title: How should India approach AI?
papers.authors: Kapur A, Narayanan A.
papers.abstract: In an unstable geopolitical environment, countries are looking to secure access to artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities, which are seen as essential to economic growth, scientific research, and national security. Few have placed sovereignty as squarely at the center of their AI strategy as India-and few are as well positioned to achieve it. But to do so, it needs to look beyond infrastructure
summary_bullets: India prioritizes AI sovereignty in geopolitics; positioned favorably but must expand beyond infrastructure focus.
AI capabilities critical for economic growth, research, and security; countries competing for strategic access.
India's AI strategy requires multifaceted approach beyond just building physical infrastructure foundations.

papers.title: Cholesterol enhances lysosome-autophagosome fusion for better α-synuclein clearance in GBA L444P-mutated Parkinson disease.
papers.authors: Chen M, Liu F, Yang Y, Chen R, Gan L, Sun Y, Yan Y, Xie S, Zhu C, Sun X, Li Y, Zhu S, Liu W, Zuo J, Yang Y, Wang J.
papers.abstract: Mutations in lysosomal enzyme glucocerebrosidase (GBA), the most common genetic risk factor for Parkinson disease (PD), exacerbate α-synuclein pathology through unclear mechanisms. Here, we report, in a large cohort, that GBA-mutated PD patients exhibit lower serum cholesterol levels. By introducing the most common GBA variant in our cohort, L444P, into human α-synuclein knock-in mice, we noted th
summary_bullets: GBA L444P mutation in PD patients correlates with reduced serum cholesterol levels and increased α-synuclein pathology.
Cholesterol enhances lysosome-autophagosome fusion, improving α-synuclein clearance in GBA-mutated cells.
Cholesterol supplementation may provide therapeutic benefit for GBA-associated Parkinson disease.

papers.title: Paclitaxel induces NM2-dependent cellular contraction through GEF-H1 dissociation from microtubules and RhoA/ROCK activation in cancer cells
papers.authors: Asensio-Juarez, G., Perez-Diaz, R., Ramos-Solano, H., Garrido-Casado, M., Talayero, V. C., Vicente-Manzanares, M.
papers.abstract: In this study, we have investigated the crosstalk between microtubule dynamics and actomyosin contractility in cancer cells treated with taxanes, which are chemotherapeutic agents used to treat solid tumors. We found that paclitaxel (PTXL) induced cell contraction through a mechanism that involved the rapid dissociation of GEF-H1 from microtubules, and the phosphorylation and acute activation of N
summary_bullets: Paclitaxel triggers cancer cell contraction via GEF-H1 release from microtubules, activating RhoA/ROCK signaling pathway.
Microtubule stabilization by paclitaxel disrupts GEF-H1 localization, leading to NM2-dependent cytoskeletal contraction in cancer cells.
Taxane chemotherapy mechanism involves crosstalk between microtubule dynamics and actomyosin contractility through RhoA signaling activation.

papers.title: Cardiomyocyte-derived Wnt5a drives doxorubicin-induced cardiomyopathy by amplifying cellular senescence
papers.authors: Sung, E.-A., Zhai, P., Ikeda, S., Matsushita, M., Takayama, K., Takada, T., Fefelova, N., Xie, L., Yehia, G., Romanienko, P., Gadiyar, V., Birge, R., Vecchio, D., Forte, M., Valenti, V., Sciarretta, S., Sadoshima, J.
papers.abstract: Doxorubicin (DOX) is an effective anthracycline chemotherapeutic agent, but its use is limited by cardiotoxicity that can progress to cardiomyopathy and heart failure. Cellular senescence contributes to DOX-induced cardiac injury, yet the upstream signals that initiate and propagate senescence in the injured heart remain unclear. Here, we identify Wnt5a, a non-canonical Wnt ligand, as a mediator o
summary_bullets: Wnt5a, secreted by cardiomyocytes, drives doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity by amplifying cellular senescence pathways.
Blocking Wnt5a signaling may represent a therapeutic strategy to prevent chemotherapy-related cardiomyopathy and heart failure.
Non-canonical Wnt/Wnt5a pathway is a previously unidentified upstream regulator of senescence in drug-injured cardiac tissue.

papers.title: Tobacco smoke-induced DNA adducts sensitize genomes to APOBEC mutagenesis and carcinogenesis through nucleotide excision repair
papers.authors: Durfee, C., Stefanovska, B., Wu, R., Cordoba-Caballero, J., Ibrahim, M. A., Carpenter, M. A., Liu, L., Nandi, S. P., Argyris, P. P., Bielo, L. B., Li, E. C. L., Temiz, N. A., Zhou, Y., Bergstrom, E. N., Mullally, C., Wang, Y., Liu, X., Barreto Duran, E., Troness, B., Proehl, J., Gupta, H., York, A., Vogel, R. I., Wells, J. M., Steele, C. D., Stuewe, I., Muldoon, D., Woo, J., Donoghue, M. T. A., Lindsey-Boltz, L. A., Sancar, A., Bandlamudi, C., Chandarlapaty, S., Yang, W., Malkova, A., Diaz-Gay, M., Alexandrov, L. B., Harris, R.
papers.abstract: Mutational processes are thought to act independently and additively. We challenge this view by demonstrating that DNA-adducting agents sensitize the genome to mutagenesis by APOBEC enzymes. A model tobacco carcinogen (NQO) triggers a 100-fold increase in APOBEC3B- catalyzed signature mutations and elevates oral carcinoma levels in vivo. A hallmark of this unidirectional synergy is strand-coordina
summary_bullets: Tobacco carcinogens sensitize genomes to APOBEC-induced mutations through nucleotide excision repair, causing 100-fold increase in mutagenesis.
DNA-adducting agents and APOBEC enzymes synergistically drive carcinogenesis rather than acting independently and additively.
Strand-coordinated mutation patterns reveal mechanistic coupling between NER pathway activation and APOBEC3B catalytic activity.

papers.title: A Unified Deep Learning-Based Framework for Reference-Based and Reference-Free Local Ancestry Inference
papers.authors: Diem, T.
papers.abstract: Local ancestry inference (LAI) identifies the ancestral origin of genomic segments within admixed individuals and is an important tool for population genetics and disease association studies. Existing LAI methods generally rely on reference panels composed of individuals from ancestral populations, limiting their applicability when such panels are unavailable or poorly characterized. We present Op
summary_bullets: Deep learning framework performs local ancestry inference both with and without reference panels, expanding applicability to understudied populations.
Unified model eliminates need for ancestral reference data while maintaining competitive accuracy with traditional reference-based methods.
Approach enables ancestry inference in admixed individuals when reference populations are unavailable or poorly characterized.

papers.title: Deep learning-guided identification of bacteriophage receptor-binding protein candidates for foodborne pathogen detection
papers.authors: Romero-Calle, D. X., Carrasco, C., Javed, B., Alexa, E.-A.
papers.abstract: Foodborne pathogens including Salmonella spp., Escherichia coli and Listeria monocytogenes cause an estimated 600 million illnesses annually. Yet conventional detection methods remain slow, costly, or insufficiently specific for routine food safety surveillance. Phage receptor-binding proteins (RBPs) are attractive recognition elements for biosensors, but their extensive sequence diversity limits
summary_bullets: Deep learning models successfully identify bacteriophage RBPs as highly specific recognition elements for rapid foodborne pathogen detection.
RBP-based biosensors overcome sequence diversity challenges, enabling faster and more cost-effective food safety surveillance alternatives.
This approach addresses limitations of conventional detection methods for Salmonella, E. coli, and Listeria monocytogenes.

papers.title: Mapping the Competence Boundary of a Protein Property Model: A Case Study on Plastic-Degrading Enzymes using ProtTrust-XAI
papers.authors: Onawole, A., Adegoke, R.
papers.abstract: Machine learning models for protein properties are usually reported by a single accuracy figure, which says how a model behaves on average but not whether to act on any one prediction, especially for a protein unlike anything in the training set. That gap is both a black box problem and an out-of-distribution problem, and it is worst exactly where discovery work happens, on sequences the model has
summary_bullets: ML protein models need competence boundaries beyond accuracy metrics to identify unreliable predictions on novel sequences.
ProtTrust-XAI framework maps where plastic-degrading enzyme models fail, improving decision-making for discovery applications.
Out-of-distribution detection is critical for protein engineering where novel sequences are the scientific target.

papers.title: Evaluating the ability of spatial transcriptomics foundation models to learn multi-scale spatial variation
papers.authors: Handa, D., Martin-Linares, C., Stein-O'Brien, G., Ling, J., Chitra, U.
papers.abstract: Spatial gene expression results from the superposition of multiple sources of variation in gene expression across different spatial scales, including local microenvironment-associated variation and global spatial gradients. Spatial foundation models (SFMs) are large-scale machine learning models trained on cohorts of spatial transcriptomics (ST) data that, in principle, learn the different sources
summary_bullets: Spatial foundation models learn multi-scale spatial variation in gene expression from local microenvironment effects to global gradients across tissues.
SFMs trained on ST data cohorts capture hierarchical sources of expression variation operating at different spatial scales simultaneously.
Foundation model approach enables learning of generalizable spatial transcriptomics patterns applicable across diverse biological contexts.

papers.title: PGViS: Personal Genome Variant interpretation Score for lung cancer genomes
papers.authors: Surana, P., Dutta, P., Boffetta, P., Davuluri, R. V.
papers.abstract: Inherited lung cancer risk arises from both protein-coding and non-coding germline variants, but the functional non-coding component is largely uncharacterized. Genome wide association studies and polygenic risk scores identify tag variants, not causal ones. Neither resolves which regulatory element is perturbed. DNA foundation models such as DNABERT decode non-coding variant effects directly from
summary_bullets: DNA foundation models can identify functional non-coding variants affecting lung cancer risk by directly decoding variant effects from sequences
PGViS integrates protein-coding and regulatory variant contributions to create comprehensive personalized lung cancer risk scores
Non-coding variants represent major uncharacterized component of inherited lung cancer susceptibility beyond traditional GWAS tag variants

papers.title: EpiBench: Can LLMs Understand Epitopes for Antibody Drug Discovery?
papers.authors: Zirui Wang, Jiaqi Wang, Qinghan Wang, Yuzhi Xu, Gang Du, Tingjun Hou, Odin Zhang
papers.abstract: Epitopes determine where antibodies bind antigens and shape downstream therapeutic properties such as functional blockade and escape resistance, making epitope understanding central to antibody drug discovery. Although large language models (LLMs) have shown strong biomedical reasoning ability, it remains unclear whether they can infer epitope information directly from antigen and antibody sequenc
summary_bullets: LLMs struggle to predict epitope information from antigen-antibody sequences alone, limiting their direct application in antibody drug discovery workflows.
EpiBench benchmark reveals performance gaps between LLMs and specialized structural prediction methods for epitope understanding tasks.
Current LLMs lack sufficient structural reasoning to infer binding site properties critical for therapeutic antibody development.

papers.title: The Virtual Tissues foundation model resolves spatial proteomics across scales
papers.authors: Wenckstern J, Jain E, von Querfurth B, Cheng Y, Vasilev K, Pariset M, Cheng PF, Liakopoulos P, Michielin O, Wicki A, Gut G, Bunne C.
papers.abstract: Spatial proteomics technologies have transformed our understanding of complex tissue architecture in cancer but present unique challenges for computational analysis<sup>1</sup>. Each study uses a different marker panel and protocol, and most methods are tailored to single cohorts, which limits knowledge transfer and robust biomarker discovery. Here we present Virtual Tissues (VirTues), a general-p
summary_bullets: VirTues foundation model enables cross-cohort spatial proteomics analysis despite different marker panels and protocols.
Single unified framework transfers knowledge across studies, improving biomarker discovery and tissue architecture understanding.
Resolves multi-scale spatial proteomics data, addressing computational challenges in cancer tissue analysis.

papers.title: A compendium of next-generation patient-derived models for diverse cancers
papers.authors: ElHarouni D, Al-Jazrawe M, Choi S, Dede M, Hinoue T, Misek SA, Noh H, Zanella L, Tseng YY, Francies HE, Plenker D, Kyi CW, Perez-Mayoral J, Stine MJ, Tonsing-Carter E, Agarwal R, Zenklusen JC, Clinton JM, Shelton JM, Chu TR, Hooper WF, Loinaz X, Keskula P, Tagle J, Kuhlers PC, Tercan B, Boj SF, Vasciaveo A, Tomassoni L, Crawford JM, Walsh S, Sinai C, Bhatia S, Sridevi P, Patel H, Cerone MA, HCMI Network, Ellrott K, Kuo CJ, Elemento O, Beyaz S, Corbo V, Spector DL, Beroukhim R, Ferguson ML, Cherniack AD, Laird PW, Robine N, McPherson A, Hoadley KA, Garnett MJ, Tuveson DA, Califano A, Spellman PT, Ligon KL, Gerhard DS, Staudt LM, Boehm JS.
papers.abstract: The development of new therapeutics and the validation of pathogenetic cancer mechanisms require representative laboratory models<sup>1,2</sup>. However, existing collections represent only a fraction of the diversity observed in human cancer<sup>2-4</sup>. Recent technologies have enabled efficient in vitro model derivation (for example, tumour organoids)<sup>5</sup>. However, whether these maint
summary_bullets: Patient-derived organoids and next-generation models now enable efficient laboratory derivation capturing broader cancer diversity than traditional cell lines.
These representative models validate pathogenic mechanisms and support therapeutic development across multiple cancer types.
New technologies provide practical tools for researchers to generate diverse cancer models reflecting human tumor heterogeneity.

papers.title: Spatial biology reveals altered macrophage states in immunosuppressed non-melanoma skin cancer
papers.authors: Naara S, Kochat V, Rao X, Arslan E, Saddawi-Konefka R, Satpati S, Garbarino J, Anderson JL, Gleber-Netto FO, Nagarajan P, Kerr TD, Akhter S, Li S, Fodor R, Koyfman SA, Yaniv D, Xie T, Glaun M, Bobian M, Padron WI, Ng C, Gunaratne PH, Thevasagayampillai S, Migden MR, Abbas HA, Reville PK, Tsai KY, McGrail DJ, Wang J, Myers JN, Gross ND, Rai K, Amit M.
papers.abstract: Immunosuppressed patients with non-melanoma skin cancer experience worse clinical outcomes, yet the tumor immune microenvironment associated with systemic immunosuppression remains incompletely defined. Using integrated single-cell, spatial transcriptomic, multiplex immunofluorescence, and spatial epigenomic profiling across immunocompetent and immunosuppressed tumors, we found that overall immune
summary_bullets: Immunosuppression alters macrophage states in non-melanoma skin cancer, contributing to worse clinical outcomes through microenvironment changes.
Spatial transcriptomics reveals distinct immune cell positioning and functional states differ between immunocompetent versus immunosuppressed tumors.
Integrated multi-omics approach identifies macrophage dysfunction as key driver of immunosuppression-related tumor progression.

papers.title: Dynamic prediction of HIV-related incomplete immune reconstitution: A multicenter, large cohort study using advanced joint modeling
papers.authors: Liu F, Zhang H, Wang X, Huang J, Shi J, Yang Z, Bao J, Zhao H, Pu C, Wang S, Xu A, Wang M, Yan D, Li Y, Sun R, Sheng H, Yu J, Zhang F, Sun L.
papers.abstract: Incomplete immune reconstitution (IIR) is a serious complication affecting 10 to 40% of people living with HIV (PLWH) despite effective antiretroviral therapy, leading to increased morbidity and mortality. Current risk prediction models rely on single-time point measurements and lack dynamic assessment capabilities. We developed a dynamic joint prediction system for IIR risk (DJPSIIR) using Bayesi
summary_bullets: Incomplete immune reconstitution affects 10-40% of people with HIV despite effective antiretroviral therapy.
Built a dynamic joint-modeling system (DJPSIIR) using repeated measurements instead of single time points.
Aims to give clinicians better, continuously updated risk prediction for IIR.

papers.title: Leveraging IGF signaling to improve the spatial organization and regenerative potential of iPSC-derived vascularized liver organoids
papers.authors: Kim DH, Lee Y, Kim MJ, Lee AC, Kwon S, Kang KS.
papers.abstract: Liver tissue engineering offers a promising alternative for end-stage liver disease, yet the recreation of functional vasculature remains a major bottleneck to clinical translation. Here, we developed vascularized liver organoids by integrating human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived hepatoblasts and endothelial cells into decellularized scaffolds functionalized with an anti-CD31 aptame
summary_bullets: Engineered vascularized liver organoids from iPSC-derived hepatoblasts and endothelial cells on functionalized scaffolds.
IGF signaling improves spatial organization of the vasculature within the organoid.
Enhances regenerative potential, a step toward liver tissue engineering for end-stage liver disease.

papers.title: Assessing pedestrian responses to autonomous and personal mobility robots in crowded public spaces
papers.authors: Wojcikiewicz D, Billard A, Paez-Granados D.
papers.abstract: Robots increasingly share spaces with people, supporting delivery services and mobility for the aging populations, yet their ability to share space comfortably lacks understanding and benchmarks for designers and policy-makers. We compared human-robot (HRI) and human-human (HHI) interactions across four real-world crowd datasets spanning Europe, North America, and Asia, using a unified pipeline to
summary_bullets: Compared human-robot and human-human interactions across four real-world crowd datasets on three continents.
Used a unified analysis pipeline to benchmark how pedestrians respond to autonomous/personal mobility robots.
Offers empirical benchmarks to guide robot design and public-space policy.

papers.title: BirdCODE: Detecting bird communication at scale
papers.authors: Fine, A., Hoffman, B., Robinson, D., Miron, M., Alizadeh, M., Chemla, E., Cusimano, M., James, L. S., Keen, S., Matthies, E., Narula, G., Nolasco, I., Geist, M.
papers.abstract: Deep learning-based animal sound identification is regularly applied to large audio datasets for ecological monitoring and citizen science, but existing methods lack the fine temporal resolution required to extract insights into animal communication from these same datasets. Here we introduce Bird Communication Detector (BirdCODE), a deep learning model that detects and classifies the vocalization
summary_bullets: BirdCODE enables fine-grained temporal detection of bird vocalizations in large audio datasets, surpassing existing methods' resolution capabilities.
Deep learning model detects and classifies individual bird communication events for ecological monitoring and citizen science applications at scale.

papers.title: Contrastive Regulatory Embeddings Attention Model for Differential Expression Prediction with Personalized Genomes: Insights and Challenges
papers.authors: Hu, Z., Ku, J., Pollard, K.
papers.abstract: Deep learning models applied to DNA sequences have achieved success in predicting gene expression, chromatin profiles, and variant pathogenicity. However, learning cross-individual differences remains challenging because DNA sequence variation between individuals is small, while gene expression is heavily influenced by non-genetic noise. Prior efforts to predict personalized gene expression from s
summary_bullets: Deep learning struggles to predict gene expression across individuals due to small DNA sequence variations and high non-genetic noise masking true regulatory effects.
Contrastive learning embeddings effectively capture regulatory differences between individuals, improving personalized expression prediction despite biological complexity.
Personalized genome models reveal fundamental challenges in disentangling genetic from environmental factors in gene regulation across populations.

papers.title: Asymmetric co-substrate usage at a metabolic branch point as a minimal network motif that can drive overflow metabolism
papers.authors: West, R., Sonal, S., Rodrigues, T. d. S. G., Shou, W., soyer, o. s.
papers.abstract: Metabolic overflow is pervasive from microbes to tumors: as glucose consumption increases, cells switch from respiration to respirofermentation with excretion of organic acids or ethanol. How do cells regulate their fluxes to implement this switch? Using simplified models of a branch point, we found that three independent "built-in" mechanisms can each enable flux switching at a branch point: diff
summary_bullets: Asymmetric co-substrate usage at metabolic branch points enables overflow metabolism without requiring complex regulation.
Three independent mechanisms can drive flux switching: differential enzyme kinetics, substrate availability, and allosteric control.
Minimal network motifs explain how cells transition from respiration to fermentation as glucose increases.

papers.title: Curved microtubule regions mark sites of lattice compaction in cells and neurons
papers.authors: Mishra, J., Volos, P., Wang, K., Birk, B., Trefftz, L., Pyrpassopoulos, S., Mohd Rafiq, N.
papers.abstract: Angstrom-scale changes in microtubule (MT) lattice spacing regulate the selective recruitment of MT-associated proteins, yet how these structural states operate in cells remains poorly understood. Here, we show that MT lattice expansion, induced by protein-based expanders or microtubule-stabilizing agents such as Taxol and epothilone D, drives the relocalization of compact lattice-binding proteins
summary_bullets: MT lattice expansion induced by expanders or stabilizing agents causes relocalization of compact lattice-binding proteins away from curved regions
Curved microtubule regions mark sites of lattice compaction that selectively recruit specific MT-associated proteins
Angstrom-scale lattice spacing changes regulate protein binding and could be therapeutic targets for MT-targeting drugs

papers.title: Endogenous APOBEC3B Promotes CHK1 Inhibitor Sensitivity
papers.authors: Stefanovska, B., Troness, B., Mullally, C., de la Pena Avalos, B., Ibrahim, M., Chen, Y., Fanunza, E., Carpenter, M., Harris, R.
papers.abstract: APOBEC3B (A3B) is a single-stranded DNA cytosine deaminase overexpressed in cancer, where it causes genomic DNA damage and mutations associated with tumor evolution. Enforced A3B overexpression triggers a dependency on the replication-stress response in different cellular models. However, whether endogenous A3B in cancer cells might yield a similar vulnerability is unclear. Here, we investigate ho
summary_bullets: Endogenous APOBEC3B in cancer cells creates replication stress, making them sensitive to CHK1 inhibition therapy.
A3B-induced DNA damage activates checkpoint pathways; blocking CHK1 prevents recovery, causing cell death in A3B-expressing cancers.
A3B expression level could predict CHK1 inhibitor response, offering potential biomarker for patient selection in treatment.

papers.title: Mechanistic and machine learning models design human gut consortia that robustly inhibit Clostridioides difficile
papers.authors: Im, H., Liu, Y., Thompson, J., Miranda, G. I., Loke, K., Bacon, R., Lucas, L., Amador-Noguez, D., Gray, S. M., Venturelli, O. S.
papers.abstract: Identifying design principles for robust inhibition of human pathogens is a major goal of microbiome engineering. By building synthetic microbial communities from the bottom-up guided by Bayesian active learning, we investigate the Clostridioides difficile growth landscape across thousands of species-metabolite conditions. Mechanistic consumer resource and machine learning models uncover significa
summary_bullets: Bayesian active learning identifies key bacterial species and metabolites that inhibit C. difficile across diverse microbiome conditions.
Consumer-resource mechanistic models combined with machine learning reveal design principles for robust pathogen suppression in synthetic communities.
Bottom-up synthetic community engineering enables predictive control of C. difficile growth in human gut microbiome systems.

papers.title: Multi-modal Graph Integration for Biologically Interpretable Domain Identification Using Spatial Transcriptomics
papers.authors: Lee, S., Wang, G., Kang, K., Chen, J., Kang, M.
papers.abstract: Functional domain identification in spatial transciptomics transforms spatial molecular measurements into mechanistic insights into tissue physiology and pathology. However, the inherent noise and sparsity of gene expression data, along with the locality-biased design of conventional graph-based approaches, fundamentally limit the accurate identification of complex tissue domains. In this study, w
summary_bullets: Multi-modal graph integration improves domain identification in spatial transcriptomics by combining multiple data modalities to overcome noise and sparsity limitations.
Novel approach addresses locality bias in conventional graph methods, enabling better detection of complex tissue domains with biological relevance.
Method transforms spatial molecular measurements into mechanistic insights for understanding tissue physiology and pathology more accurately.

papers.title: Graph Machine Learning for Physiological Role Prediction in Protein Contact Networks: A Large-Scale Comparative Study on the Human Proteome
papers.authors: Cervellini, M., Martino, A.
papers.abstract: Proteins are fundamental macromolecules involved in virtually all biological processes. Their physiological roles are tightly linked to their three-dimensional structure, which can be naturally abstracted as Protein Contact Networks (PCNs), i.e., graphs where residues are nodes and edges encode spatial proximity. This representation enables the application of graph machine learning to address the
summary_bullets: Graph neural networks effectively predict protein physiological roles from contact network structure across large-scale human proteome datasets.
Protein contact networks as graph representations bridge structural information to functional annotations better than alternative approaches.
Comparative study establishes benchmarks for applying graph ML methods to protein function prediction tasks.

papers.title: Mapping the Human Ghost Proteome: Classification and Experimental Detection Biases in the Identification of Alternative Microproteins
papers.authors: Montero-Calle, A., Pelaez-Garcia, A., Martin-Galiano, A. J., Barderas, R.
papers.abstract: The discovery of alternative proteins (AltProts), translated from non-canonical ORFs, has expanded the human proteome and revealed a hidden layer known as the "ghost proteome". Despite increasing evidence, AltProts detection remains challenging due to their small size, physicochemical heterogeneity, and lack of annotation. Here, we developed an integrated bioinformatic and proteomic workflow to be
summary_bullets: Alternative proteins from non-canonical ORFs expand the human proteome but remain difficult to detect due to small size and poor annotation.
Integrated bioinformatic and proteomic workflow enables systematic detection of ghost proteome with improved classification of alternative microproteins.
Detection biases exist in alternative protein identification; study maps these limitations for more comprehensive proteome characterization.

papers.title: A Comprehensive Database of Simulations and Meshes of Coronary Arteries from the Fame 2 Trial
papers.authors: Marcinno', F., Hinz, J., Ando', E., Mahendiran, T., Buffa, A., Deparis, S.
papers.abstract: AO_SCPLOWBSTRACTC_SCPLOWIn this work, we publish the 3D unsteady Navier-Stokes numerical simulations and meshes of coronary arteries reconstructed from invasive X-ray coronary angiograms acquired during in the Fractional Flow Reserve versus Angiography for Multivessel Evaluation 2 (FAME 2) trial. Out of the 914 clinical images, 779 vessels are successfully reconstructed and meshed. The remaining 1
summary_bullets: Large database of 779 coronary artery reconstructions from FAME 2 trial with validated 3D CFD simulations publicly available for research.
High-quality meshes and unsteady Navier-Stokes simulations enable studies of coronary hemodynamics and vessel physiology.
Resource supports development of computational methods for clinical assessment of coronary artery disease.

papers.title: Distinct cellular phenotypes of language and executive decline in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
papers.authors: Petrescu J, Gouveia Roque C, Jackson CA, Daly AC, Butti Z, Kang K, Casel O, Leung M, Reilly L, Eschbach J, Gebremedhin B, McDade K, Gregory JM, Bonneau R, Smith C, Phatnani H.
papers.abstract: Cognitive manifestations, including impairments in language and executive functions, are seen in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We mapped prefrontal cortex regions from ALS patients by integrating spatial and single-nucleus transcriptomics in a cognitively stratified patient cohort. We uncover that cognitive impairment in ALS is associated with d
summary_bullets: Mapped prefrontal cortex regions in ALS patients using combined spatial and single-nucleus transcriptomics.
Cognitive impairment (language/executive decline) in ALS is associated with distinct cellular changes.
Stratified cohort by cognitive status to link specific cell states to specific symptoms.

papers.title: Divergent impacts of explainable AI for dermatological diagnosis on clinicians versus lay people
papers.authors: Xu X', Hu H, Zhang H, Wang WK, Wang R, Soenksen LR, Badri O, Jafry S, Burger E, Nwandu L, Mehta A, Duhaime EP, Qasim A, Lin H, Pereira JK, Hershon J, Mui P, Gru AA, Elhadad N, Mamykina L, Groh M, Tschandl P, Daneshjou R, Ghassemi M.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly permeating healthcare, from serving as a physician assistant to powering consumer applications. The opacity of AI algorithms makes the ability of humans to interact with AI algorithms challenging. To overcome this limitation, explainable AI (XAI) provides insight into AI decision-making, but evidence suggests that XAI can paradoxically induce bias in th
summary_bullets: Explainable AI (XAI) is meant to make AI decisions more transparent in dermatology diagnosis.
XAI has divergent effects: it can help or paradoxically bias interpretation depending on the user.
Clinicians and lay people respond very differently to the same AI explanations.

papers.title: Follicular Lymphoma Transformation is Characterized by Cytokine-associated Remodeling of Stromal and Macrophage Compartments.
papers.authors: Haradhvala NJ, Yiu SPT, Beckmann L, Sadigh S, Leibowitz Z, Landolsi E, Rivero S, Deng SL, Hu S, Zhang M, Filip D, Pospistle A, Yeo YY, Maurer K, Gustafsson J, Stewart K, Shanmugam V, Van Orden M, Lu WS, Li S, Livak KJ, Qiu H, Basak A, Shalek AK, Danysh BP, McDonough M, Gohil SH, Ren Y, Zhou Y, Neuberg DS, Tyekucheva S, Rodig SJ, Jacobsen ED, Mraz M, Murakami MA, Kurt H, Wu CJ, Getz G, Jiang S, Parry EM.
papers.abstract: Across cancer, one of the most frequent examples of histologic transformation is the evolution of follicular lymphoma (FL) to an aggressive large cell lymphoma. Despite recent progress, understanding of the molecular and cellular underpinnings of transformation remains incomplete. Here, we dissect the interplay of tumor and microenvironment cell populations across transformation through a multimod
summary_bullets: Multimodal profiling dissects tumor-microenvironment interplay during transformation of follicular lymphoma to aggressive large-cell lymphoma.
Transformation is characterized by cytokine-driven remodeling of stromal and macrophage compartments.
Identifies microenvironmental changes as active drivers, not just bystanders, of lymphoma transformation.

papers.title: Want to get more from AI? Treat every prompt like an experiment
papers.authors: Dewar JM.
summary_bullets: Nature commentary argues researchers should approach AI prompting with the same rigor as a scientific experiment.
Encourages systematic testing and iteration to get more reliable, useful outputs from AI tools.

papers.title: Uncovering ectopic GC-like niches for tumor reactive lymphocyte priming in lung adenocarcinoma using Stereo-XCR-seq
papers.authors: Zhan X, Huang M, Zhang Y, Liu Z, Liu C, Guo Y, Liu Y, Zhou W, Yan Y, Zeng H, Dong Y, Dong X, Chen X, Yang H, Ma R, Zhu F, Zheng X, Li X, Hou S, Gao Z, Yin J, Chan FK, Wu Q, Deng S, Yao Y, Suo S, Liu C, Liu L, Xu X, Hou Y, Tao H, Ai X, Dong Y, Zeng T, Sun H, Li Y, Zuo L, Wang H, Liu X, Wu Z, Zhou J, Zeng Z, Feng Y.
papers.abstract: T/B cell receptors (T/BCR), coordinating antigen-targeting immune response, play crucial roles in anti-tumor immune response. Tracking T and B cell clonal evolution in situ at single-cell resolution is essential for understanding the adaptive immune responses. To address the lack of tools for in situ single-cell T/BCR (XCR) sequencing, we develop Stereo-XCR-seq, an efficient method for retrieving
summary_bullets: Develops Stereo-XCR-seq, an in situ single-cell method for spatially resolved T/B-cell receptor (TCR/BCR) sequencing.
Reveals ectopic germinal-center-like niches in lung adenocarcinoma that prime tumor-reactive lymphocytes.
Enables tracking of clonal immune cell evolution directly within the tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: A foundation model for sleep-based risk stratification and clinical outcomes
papers.authors: Bilal E, Araujo MLD, Beck KL, Heinzinger CM, Ghosn S, Saab CY, Foldvary-Schaefer N, Rogers JL, Mehra R.
papers.abstract: Clinical sleep studies capture multiple physiologic signals, yet interpretation is often reduced to single summary measures of limited prognostic value, such as the apnea-hypopnea index. We present a foundation model that learns rich representations of sleep physiology from more than 10,000 clinical sleep recordings linked to electronic medical records. Here we show that sleep physiology contains
summary_bullets: Built a foundation model trained on over 10,000 clinical sleep recordings linked to electronic medical records.
Moves beyond single summary metrics (like apnea-hypopnea index) to richer sleep-physiology representations.
Enables better risk stratification and prediction of clinical outcomes from sleep data.

papers.title: Ultrarapid deep 3D histology enables intraoperative mapping of glioma infiltration
papers.authors: Liu Z, Li Y, Chen L, Wei M, Wei M, Sun Y, Wang T, Cheng H, Liu X, Ji M, Shi L.
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) histology provides volumetric insights into tissue microarchitectures across entire specimens, holding great promise for more accurate prognostication. However, existing methods are too slow for intraoperative consultations. We present ULTRA (ultrarapid cleared stimulated Raman with AI), a label-free, stain-free, fixation-free, and section-free platform that leverages the ch
summary_bullets: ULTRA is a label-free, stain-free, fixation-free 3D histology platform using stimulated Raman scattering plus AI.
Fast enough for intraoperative use, unlike existing 3D histology methods.
Enables real-time mapping of glioma infiltration margins during surgery.

papers.title: Privacy risks from medical AI tools are not shared equally
papers.authors: Zhang H, Ghassemi M.
summary_bullets: Nature commentary highlights that privacy risks from medical AI tools fall disproportionately on certain patient groups.
Calls attention to equity considerations often overlooked in medical AI deployment and data use.

papers.title: This AI Raygun can shrink and supersize proteins - opening the door to easy editing
papers.authors: Conroy G.
summary_bullets: News piece on "Raygun," an AI tool that can shrink or enlarge natural proteins while preserving function.
Framed as opening new possibilities for easier, more flexible protein engineering.

papers.title: SPEN Loss Drives Extrafollicular Diffuse Large B-cell Lymphoma with Female-Specific Lethality and Therapeutic Vulnerabilities
papers.authors: Pelzer B, Meydan C, Spiegel IM, Karagiannidis I, Xia M, Teater M, Welter EM, Searcy ZE, Hilton LK, Barisic D, Fong A, Fa P, Sethi S, Isgor IS, Fielding JJ, Karbalayghareh A, Burdette CS, Tumuluru S, Debek SM, Lee S, Massoni-Badosa R, Durmaz C, Salataj E, Pararajalingam P, Chen Z, Pelzl RJ, Shah S, Rivas MA, Hoehn KB, Mlynarczyk C, Isles HM, Wang X, Dogan A, Elenitoba-Johnson KSJ, Scott DW, Dreval K, Morin RD, Leslie CS, Puri R, Geri JB, Chin CR, Chadburn A, Mason CE, Reinhardt HC, Anguera MC, Béguelin W, Venturutti L, Melnick AM.
papers.abstract: Diffuse large B-cell lymphomas (DLBCL) are genetically and phenotypically heterogeneous, making diagnosis and treatment challenging. Current models suggest DLBCLs derive from follicular B cells engaged in adaptive immune responses. By studying cooccurring truncating mutations in SPEN and NOTCH2 in the BN2-DLBCL subtype, our data suggest a previously unrecognized extrafollicular trajectory. Using a
summary_bullets: SPEN and NOTCH2 co-occurring truncating mutations define a previously unrecognized extrafollicular DLBCL trajectory.
This SPEN-loss DLBCL subtype shows female-specific lethality.
Identifies therapeutic vulnerabilities specific to this newly defined lymphoma subtype.

papers.title: Same-Slide Spatial Multiomics Integration with IN-DEPTH Reveals Tumor Virus-Linked Spatial Reorganization of the Tumor Microenvironment
papers.authors: Yiu SPT, Chang Y, Yeo YY, Qiu H, Wu W, Michel HA, Jin X, Huang R, Kure S, Parmelee L, Luo S, Cramer P, Lee JL, Wang Y, Zhao Z, Yeung J, El Ahmar N, Simsek B, Mohanna R, Van Orden M, Lu WS, Livak KJ, Li S, Gao C, Burgess M, Keane C, Shahryari J, Kingsley LG, Al-Humadi RN, Nasr S, Nkosi D, Sadigh S, Rock P, Frauenfeld L, Kaufmann L, Zhu B, Basak A, Dhanikonda N, Chan CN, Krull J, Cho YW, Chen CY, Brown J, Wang H, Zhao B, Lee JJ, Loo LH, Kim DM, Boussiotis VA, Zhang B, Wei K, Shalek AK, Howitt BE, Signoretti S, Schürch CM, Hodi FS, Burack WR, Rodig SJ, Ma Q, Jiang S.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics and proteomics have enabled profound insights into tissue organization, yet these technologies remain largely disparate, and emerging same-slide multiomics approaches are limited in plex, spatial resolution, signal retention, and integrative analytics. We introduce IN-situ DEtailed Phenotyping To High-resolution transcriptomics (IN-DEPTH), a streamlined, resource-efficient,
summary_bullets: IN-DEPTH combines spatial transcriptomics and proteomics on the same tissue slide, improving on disparate single-modality methods.
Reveals tumor-virus-linked spatial reorganization of the tumor microenvironment.
Designed to be streamlined and resource-efficient for broader adoption.

papers.title: CellTune: an integrative software for accurate cell classification in spatial proteomics
papers.authors: Bussi Y, Shainshein D, Ovits E, Posner S, Azulay N, Maimon N, Keidar Haran T, Ben-Uri R, Brown C, Schuldiner N, Yaniv E, Van Valen D, Milo I, Elhanani O, Schiemann R, Keren L.
papers.abstract: Spatial proteomics measures multiple proteins in situ, capturing tissue complexity. However, cell classification in densely packed tissues remains challenging because of the lack of efficient classification algorithms, annotation tools and high-quality labeled datasets to benchmark computational methods. We introduce CellTune, an integrated software for analysis of large spatial proteomics dataset
summary_bullets: CellTune is integrative software for accurate cell classification in densely packed spatial proteomics data.
Addresses the lack of efficient algorithms, annotation tools, and benchmark datasets in the field.
Aims to standardize and improve cell-type calling across spatial proteomics platforms.

papers.title: SpaMTP: integrative statistical analysis and visualization of spatial metabolomics and transcriptomics data
papers.authors: Causer A, Lu T, Kriel J, Moffet JJD, Fitzgerald CCJ, Newman A, Vu H, Tan X, Vo T, Cui C, Narayana VK, Whittle JR, Best SA, Freytag S, Nguyen Q.
papers.abstract: Spatially resolved multimodal data enable the exploration of transcriptional, proteomic and metabolic regulation, yet analytical tools to integrate these spatial omics modalities, particularly spatial metabolomics, remain limited. We developed SpaMTP, an end-to-end framework that implements functions within a common Seurat architecture. It introduces analyses for metabolite annotation, joint clust
summary_bullets: SpaMTP integrates spatial metabolomics and transcriptomics analysis within the familiar Seurat framework.
Adds tools for metabolite annotation, joint clustering, and cross-modality visualization.
Fills a gap left by existing tools that don't handle spatial metabolomics well.

papers.title: Author Correction: Cucurbituril-based anion-conducting membranes with supramolecular nanopores
papers.authors: Xu Z, Lin D, Yin H, Feng Q, Foglia F, Zhen Y, Morris A, Berrod Q, Pang M, Huang L, Liu J, Tian J, Wang X, Yang C, Tang X, Zhang X, Wang B, Wang H, Liu K.
summary_bullets: Published correction to a paper on cucurbituril-based anion-conducting membranes with supramolecular nanopores.
No new scientific findings; amends or clarifies details of the original report.

papers.title: End-to-end multimodal pathology foundation model with clinical dialogue
papers.authors: Vorontsov E, Shaikovski G, Casson A, Viret J, Zimmermann E, Tenenholtz N, Wang YK, Bernhard JH, Godrich RA, Retamero JA, Shia J, Gonen M, Weiser MR, Klimstra DS, Yousfi R, Fusi N, Fuchs TJ, Severson K, Liu S.
papers.abstract: Recent rapid progress in the field of computational pathology has been enabled by foundation models. These models are beginning to move beyond encoding image patches toward whole-slide understanding, but their clinical utility remains limited. Here we present PRISM2, a multimodal slide-level foundation model trained on 2.3 million whole-slide images and 14 million question-answer pairs derived fro
summary_bullets: PRISM2 is a multimodal, slide-level pathology foundation model trained on 2.3M whole-slide images and 14M Q&A pairs.
Moves beyond patch-level image encoding toward whole-slide, dialogue-capable understanding.
Aims to improve clinical utility of computational pathology through interactive, clinically grounded outputs.

papers.title: Scientists using LLMs will 'do more, less well', modelling study predicts
papers.authors: Glickman K.
summary_bullets: Modelling study predicts scientists using LLMs will increase output but reduce quality/rigor per study.
Raises concerns about an AI-driven productivity/quality trade-off in research.

papers.title: Mapping micrometastatic seeds of relapse
papers.authors: Yeo HTG, Tan IB.
papers.abstract: In this issue of Cancer Cell, Liu et al. apply spatial multi-omics to map colorectal cancer micrometastases across primary tumors and matched liver and lung metastases, revealing liver micrometastases as an early evolved, stem-like, immune-suppressed residual disease state linked to a six-gene recurrence signature.
summary_bullets: Commentary on a study applying spatial multi-omics to colorectal cancer micrometastases in liver and lung.
Liver micrometastases appear as an early, stem-like, immune-suppressed residual disease state.
This state links to a six-gene signature predicting recurrence risk.

papers.title: Spatial atlas of the human brain vasculature reveals specialized cell ensembles
papers.authors: Wang JC, Sanchez D, Arul S, Gülsuyu B, Gopinadhan A, Mukhtar T, Kim J, Andrews JP, Alonso Cee Williams M, Jung Y, Hashimoto ML, Kim CN, Bhalla S, Ewing-Crystal NA, Bernabei JM, Letchuman V, Haddad AF, Hemphill K, Weinsheimer SM, Kim H, Narsinh KH, Cooke DL, Cadwell CR, Wälchli T, Elahi FM, Yang AC, He P, Chang EF, Molofsky AB, Winkler EA.
papers.abstract: The brain vasculature comprises diverse specialized cells that are essential for brain function, yet their spatial organization remains poorly understood. Here, we construct a comprehensive cerebrovascular cell atlas encompassing 314,535 transcriptomes that captures the arteriovenous axis and defines consensus cell states. We then perform spatial transcriptomics to map 1,529,740 cells across the h
summary_bullets: Built a cerebrovascular cell atlas of over 314,000 transcriptomes spanning the human brain's arteriovenous axis.
Spatial transcriptomics mapped over 1.5 million cells to their vascular locations across the brain.
Reveals specialized, spatially organized vascular cell ensembles supporting brain function.

papers.title: AI-driven discovery and validation of a GIPC1 PDZ domain inhibitor for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
papers.authors: Rachamala HK, Rao Nakka NM, Angom RS, Varanasi SM, Wei F, Kulkarni T, Dutta SK, Wang E, Kulkarni NM, Geoffrey A S B, Hegde SP, Perumal S, Gurram K, Gharibi H, Gaetani M, Mukherjee SP, Babiker H, Pal K, Mukhopadhyay D.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains highly aggressive, with a five-year survival rate under 13.3%, due to late diagnosis, rapid progression, and therapeutic resistance, highlighting the need for advanced treatments. GAIP-interacting protein C terminus 1 (GIPC1), a scaffolding protein overexpressed in PDAC, drives tumor growth and chemoresistance but has remained "undruggable" due to it
summary_bullets: GIPC1, an "undruggable" scaffolding protein, drives PDAC tumor growth and chemoresistance.
Used AI-driven discovery to find a small-molecule inhibitor targeting GIPC1's PDZ domain.
Validates a new therapeutic candidate for a cancer with under 13.3% five-year survival.

papers.title: Human-inspired time-series health evaluation with an adaptive multimodal electronic skin
papers.authors: Xu C, Zheng H, Heng W, Liu R, MarionSims J, Li J, Jin P, Tay RY, Min J, Wang G, Yue Y, Gao W.
papers.abstract: Electronic skin powered with artificial intelligence could enable next-generation robotic and medical devices, yet integrating multimodal sensors and analyzing heterogeneous, multifrequency time series remain challenging. Most wearable machine learning architectures are time-invariant and trained for a specific task, limiting transfer across modalities and users. We present a multimodal electronic
summary_bullets: Developed a multimodal, AI-powered electronic skin for time-series health monitoring.
Adaptive architecture transfers across sensing modalities and users, unlike prior time-invariant wearable ML.
Enables human-inspired, continuous health evaluation for next-gen wearable and robotic devices.

papers.title: Inference of secreted protein signaling activities in intercellular communication
papers.authors: Ru B, Gong L, Yang E, Park S, Zaki G, Aldape K, Wakefield L, Jiang P.
papers.abstract: The human genome encodes ~1,900 secreted proteins, many of which mediate intercellular communication. Secreted proteins do not act cell-autonomously, limiting systematic approaches to characterize their functions. Here we introduce SecAct (Secreted Activity, https://secact.ccr.cancer.gov ), a computational framework that infers the signaling activities of 1,170 human secreted proteins from spatial
summary_bullets: SecAct infers signaling activity of 1,170 human secreted proteins from spatial and transcriptomic data.
Addresses the challenge that secreted proteins act non-cell-autonomously, complicating standard analysis.
Provides a computational framework and public tool for studying intercellular communication via secreted factors.

papers.title: Author Correction: Sleep chart of biological ageing clocks in middle and late life
papers.authors: MULTI Consortium, O'Toole CK, Song Z, Anagnostakis F, Yang Z, Tian YE, Duggan MR, Zou C, Leng Y, Cai Y, Bai W, Fu CHY, Rafii MS, Aisen P, Wang G, De Jager PL, Zeng J, Oh HS, Zhou X, Walker KA, Belsky DW, Zalesky A, Simonsick EM, Resnick SM, Ferrucci L, Davatzikos C, Wen J.
summary_bullets: Published correction to a large multi-cohort study of biological ageing clocks across middle and late life sleep.
Amends details of the original "sleep chart of biological ageing clocks" report.

papers.title: Mediators of cell fate decisions in human fetal kidney development identified using spatial transcriptomics
summary_bullets: Nature Genetics piece on mediators of cell fate decisions in human fetal kidney development, identified via spatial transcriptomics.
Companion to related work directly mapping kidney developmental cell-fate decisions.

papers.title: Single-cell spatial mapping of human kidney development implicates the microenvironment in guiding cell fate decisions
papers.authors: Levinsohn J, Grindel S, Dumoulin B, Abedini A, Conte C, Huang AZ, Levin-Klein R, Weisz B, Rabinowitz G, Bergeson AM, Ha E, Klötzer KA, Zhang N, Titchenell P, Li M, Park JS, Arroyo JP, Finn LS, Sasaki K, Beckerman P, Pleniceanu O, Romagnani P, Hughes AJ, Susztak K.
papers.abstract: Evolution has used cell-cell communication as a strategy to coordinate organ development, enabling the reproducible generation of intricate structures. Classically, these interactions have been studied one at a time in model organisms, limiting our understanding of how cellular interplay coordinates human development. We investigated human kidney development using single-cell RNA sequencing and sp
summary_bullets: Single-cell RNA-seq plus spatial profiling of human kidney development reveals cell-cell communication driving fate decisions.
Shows the microenvironment actively guides which cell fates progenitor cells adopt.
Moves beyond model-organism studies to directly characterize human kidney developmental signaling.

papers.title: Decadal sink-source shifts of forest aboveground carbon since 1988
papers.authors: Qian Z, Bathiany S, Liu T, Blaschke LL, Teo HC, Boers N.
papers.abstract: Forest ecosystems are vital to the global carbon cycle, yet their long-term aboveground carbon (AGC) dynamics remain uncertain. Here, we integrate multi-source satellite observations with probabilistic deep learning models to reconstruct a harmonized, uncertainty-aware global forest AGC record from 1988 to 2021 at 0.25<sup>∘</sup>. We find that, although global forests sequestered 6.2 PgC, moist t
summary_bullets: Combined satellite data with probabilistic deep learning to reconstruct global forest carbon dynamics from 1988-2021.
Global forests sequestered 6.2 PgC overall, but moist tropical forests show shifting sink/source behavior.
Provides an uncertainty-aware, long-term record of how forest carbon storage is changing.

papers.title: Escaping our own biases: AI, scientific reasoning, and discovery in molecular biology
papers.authors: Costa TRD, Penadés JR.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence may transform molecular biology not by always providing the correct answer, but by exploring mechanistic possibilities unconstrained by the assumptions that shape expert thinking. Its greatest contribution may be exposing the intellectual blind spots of scientists, while experimental validation remains the ultimate arbiter of truth.
summary_bullets: Commentary argues AI's value in molecular biology may lie in exploring possibilities beyond expert assumptions, not just giving correct answers.
AI can expose scientists' intellectual blind spots, but experiments remain the final arbiter of truth.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal multiomics uncover tumor ecosystem dynamics during metastatic colonization
papers.authors: Sun Y, Zhong Y, Liu S, Zhang Z, Wang C, Liu Y, Chen J, Guo W, Gu X, Rao K, Wang Z, Cao M, Wang Y, Huang W, Zou X, Chen X, Qiu S, Shi Y, Sun H, Huang X, Wang Y, Wang J, Wu Z, Tian R, Zhang Y, Gu J, Jiang M, Bai Y, Li G, Xie M, Xi F, Peng L, Liu S, Yang S, Zhang Y, Esteban MA, Jin X, Chen A, Wang J, Cang Y, Peng DH, Xu X, Zhou J, Wu L, Fan J.
papers.abstract: The mechanisms underlying the interactions between disseminated tumor cells (DTCs) and their tissue microenvironment during metastatic colonization are currently poorly understood. We integrated multimodal single-cell and spatial profiling from liver cancer mouse models and human metastases to track the spatiotemporal dynamics of DTCs and their microenvironments from single-cell seeding to overt l
summary_bullets: Integrated single-cell and spatial profiling of liver cancer mouse models and human metastases.
Tracks disseminated tumor cells and their microenvironment from single-cell seeding to overt metastasis.
Reveals dynamic tumor-microenvironment interactions driving metastatic colonization over time.

papers.title: Gene regulatory innovations from transposable elements in primate cerebellum development
papers.authors: Yamada T, Sepp M, Sarropoulos I, Kaessmann H.
papers.abstract: Transposable elements are hypothesized to have driven gene regulatory innovation, yet their contributions to primate brain development at the cell type level remain underexplored. Here, we use single-cell multiomics data from human, macaque, marmoset, and mouse cerebella to show that transposable element contributions to different cell types are shaped by varying degrees of constraints across cell
summary_bullets: Compared single-cell multiomics across human, macaque, marmoset, and mouse cerebellum development.
Transposable elements contribute to gene regulatory innovation in a cell-type-specific manner.
Degree of TE-driven regulatory contribution varies with evolutionary constraint across cell types.
